question: What host filesystem boundary should OpenClaw expose: deny-wins `tools.fs` allow/deny paths, `tools.fs.roots` access modes, or workspace-only plus a separate exec path policy?
rationale: The choice defines a public config surface and security boundary, and open candidate PRs show incompatible designs with different false-security and compatibility tradeoffs.

options.title: Settle one tools.fs path-policy contract
options.body: Choose the canonical config shape, require normalization/symlink/deny-precedence tests, and make exec coverage explicit before merging an implementation.

options.title: Split exec from file-tool policy
options.body: Allow a file-tool-only policy only if docs and issue tracking clearly state shell-mediated filesystem access remains a separate boundary.

options.title: Stay with workspace/sandbox isolation
options.body: Reject host path ACLs beyond `workspaceOnly` and sandbox backends if maintainers decide OpenClaw should not own that boundary.

recommendation.title: Settle one tools.fs path-policy contract
recommendation.body: Choose the canonical config shape, require normalization/symlink/deny-precedence tests, and make exec coverage explicit before merging an implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest combined signal from prior review discussion and history introducing/centralizing the current workspaceOnly policy.
